questions.text: Explain what overfitting is and give two ways to reduce it.
questions.model_answer: Overfitting is when a model fits noise in the training data and generalises poorly to unseen data (high variance: low train error, high test error). Remedies: more data, regularisation (L1/L2, dropout), early stopping, simpler model, cross-validation.

criteria.name: Defines overfitting
criteria.description: Model fits training noise / poor generalisation to unseen data

criteria.name: Mentions train/test gap
criteria.description: Low training error but high test/validation error

criteria.name: Two remedies
criteria.description: Any two valid remedies (regularisation, more data, early stopping, dropout...)

questions.text: Write the gradient descent update rule and explain the role of the learning rate.
questions.model_answer: theta := theta - alpha * grad J(theta). A small learning rate converges slowly; too large a rate overshoots or diverges.

criteria.name: Update rule
criteria.description: Correct update with gradient and step size

criteria.name: Learning rate effect
criteria.description: Explains too small = slow, too large = overshoot/diverge

questions.text: What is the purpose of the softmax function?
questions.model_answer: Softmax converts a vector of logits into a probability distribution (non-negative, sums to 1), typically for multi-class classification outputs.

criteria.name: Probability distribution
criteria.description: Outputs sum to 1 / interpretable as probabilities
